0.x: Salt = a **daily necessity of rich and poor alike**; the tax (at times 14 times the value) and the **state monopoly** showed the most oppressive face of British rule.
Gandhi: the government even **destroyed naturally formed salt** to stop untaxed use – it had no right to destroy what nature produced.
**Immediate issue:** salt tax / monopoly; **ultimate goal:** **Purna Swaraj**.

r: **78 followers** (79 with Gandhi; often rounded to "80"); the largest group (about half) from **Gujarat**
**About 240 miles (~385-390 km)** in **24 days**, entirely on foot
**Dandi**, a coastal village in **Navsari district**, Gujarat
**5 April 1930** – "**I want world sympathy in this battle of Right against Might**" (message to the press, 5.4.1930)
**6 April 1930** – Gandhi picked up a lump of natural salt on the beach; the **CDM formally began**

0.x: **"Sedition has become my religion":** said during the Salt March (**Borsad speech, 18 March 1930** – "I have made sedition my dharma").
**Subhas Bose** likened the march to **Napoleon's march from Elba to Paris**; the **US press (Time)** followed it – Time named Gandhi Man of the Year (1931).
**Arrest:** night of **4-5 May 1930** at Karadi; lodged in **Yerwada Jail**; successors **Abbas Tyabji** (1st), then **Sarojini Naidu** (2nd).
Gandhi set out from Sabarmati but **launched** the CDM at **Dandi** on **6 April 1930**.

1.x: **Calcutta session (Dec 1928, president Motilal Nehru):** accepted the Nehru Report (Dominion Status) with a **one-year ultimatum** – if Dominion Status was not granted by **31 December 1929**, Congress would adopt **complete independence** and launch civil disobedience.

**Irwin's (Deepavali) Declaration, 31 Oct 1929:** Dominion Status as the goal, no timeline; promised a Round Table Conference. The **Delhi Manifesto** (2 Nov 1929) demands were rejected in December 1929.

r: **Jawaharlal Nehru** – his **first** Congress presidency (backed by Gandhi though most PCCs opposed him); succeeded his father Motilal (1928)
Nehru **hoisted the newly adopted tricolour at midnight, 31 Dec 1929, on the banks of the Ravi**
"We have now an open conspiracy to free this country from foreign rule"
**Purna Swaraj (complete independence)**; the **Nehru Report / Dominion Status** scheme declared lapsed
**Congress Working Committee authorised to launch civil disobedience** (including non-payment of taxes); members of legislatures asked to resign
**26 January 1930** fixed as the **first Independence (Purna Swaraj) Day**, to be observed every year

1.x: The abolition of untouchability was not a Lahore resolution; the NCM was launched in 1920.
**26 January 1950** was chosen for the Constitution because Congress had celebrated **26 January 1930** as the first Independence Day.

**Andhra:** **Bulusu Sambamurthy (East Godavari)** got a Purna Swaraj resolution passed at the district level first.
**Lahore 1929** = Jawaharlal Nehru = Purna Swaraj, **31 Dec 1929**, flag on the Ravi → Independence Day **26 January 1930**.

r: His arrest led to mass demonstrations in **Peshawar** (Qissa Khwani firing); the city was in the crowds' hands for over a week

4.x: The CDM was the **first nationalist movement with women in large numbers** (picketing liquor and foreign-cloth shops); the **Salt Satyagraha** saw the maximum women's participation. **Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** persuaded Gandhi to admit women.
